title: 2013 AMC 12A Problem 15
statement: Rabbits Peter and Pauline have three offspring—Flopsie, Mopsie, and Cottontail. These five rabbits are to be distributed to four different pet stores so that no store gets both a parent and a child. It is not required that every store gets a rabbit. In how many different ways can this be done?

solutions.text:
If the two parents share a store, there are \(4\) choices for it, and each child must go to one of the other three stores: \(4\cdot 3^3 = 108\) ways.

If the parents go to different stores, there are \(4\cdot 3 = 12\) choices, and each child must go to one of the two remaining stores: \(12\cdot 2^3 = 96\) ways.

The total is \(108 + 96 = 204.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Split into cases by whether the two parents go to the same store
Same store: \(4\) parent choices and \(3^3\) child assignments; different stores: \(4\cdot 3\) and \(2^3\)
